def test_top_paths():
    # Test top_paths function
    entries = [
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/contact'},
        {'path': '/index.html'},
        {'path': '/about'},
        {'path': '/api/data?param=value'},
        {'path': '/api/data?other=param'},
        {'path': '/api/data'},
    ]
    
    result = s2_logs.top_paths(entries)
    expected = [('/index.html', 3), ('/about', 2), ('/api/data', 2), ('/contact', 1)]
    
    # Check that we get the right paths and counts
    assert len(result) == 4, f"Expected 4 paths, got {len(result)}"
    
    # Check the first three (most frequent)
    assert result[0] == ('/index.html', 3), f"Expected ('/index.html', 3), got {result[0]}"
    assert result[1] == ('/about', 2), f"Expected ('/about', 2), got {result[1]}"
    assert result[2] == ('/api/data', 2), f"Expected ('/api/data', 2), got {result[2]}"
    
    # Check that query strings are ignored
    # Both '/api/data?param=value' and '/api/data?other=param' should count as '/api/data'
    
    # Test with n=2
    result_2 = s2_logs.top_paths(entries, n=2)
    assert len(result_2) == 2, f"Expected 2 paths, got {len(result_2)}"
    assert result_2[0] == ('/index.html', 3), f"Expected ('/index.html', 3), got {result_2[0]}"
    assert result_2[1] == ('/about', 2), f"Expected ('/about', 2), got {result_2[1]}"
    
    # Test with empty list
    empty_result = s2_logs.top_paths([])
    assert empty_result == [], f"Expected empty list, got {empty_result}"
    
    print("top_paths test passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_parse_log()
    test_bad_lines()
    test_empty_and_blank_lines()
    test_status_counts()
    test_error_rate()
    test_top_paths()
    print("All tests passed!")
